name: Laboratory safety rules and hazard symbols

questions.q: What is the most important rule when entering a science laboratory?
a: Listen to the teacher and follow instructions

questions.q: Which hazard symbol indicates that a substance can cause skin or eye irritation?
What should you do if you spill a chemical on your skin?
a: Tell the teacher and wash with plenty of water

questions.q: Which symbol represents a substance that is highly flammable and must be kept away from open flames?
Why is it forbidden to eat or drink in the laboratory?
a: Because the food might get cold
To prevent accidental ingestion of chemicals

questions.q: What does the 'Corrosive' hazard symbol (showing test tubes spilling on hand and surface) warn you about?
a: The substance can damage eyes, skin, and materials

questions.q: What should you do with long hair during a practical experiment?
Which symbol warns that a substance is 'Toxic' and can be poisonous?
When heating substances in a test tube, where should the opening of the tube point?
What should you wear to protect your eyes during experiments involving chemicals?
What is the correct way to smell a chemical in the lab?
a: Put your nose right into the beaker
Use your hand to 'waft' the fumes toward you
Ask a friend to smell it first

questions.q: Which hazard symbol indicates an 'Environmental Hazard' that can harm aquatic life?
What should you do if you break glassware in the laboratory?
a: Pick it up with your fingers

questions.q: Why is it important to wash your hands after a laboratory experiment?
a: To make the sink look clean

questions.q: Which symbol represents 'Oxidizing' substances that can intensify fires?
What should you do before starting any experiment?
Where should you dispose of broken glass?
What does the 'Biohazard' symbol warn of?
a: Biological substances that may pose a health risk

questions.q: What should you wear on your feet in the laboratory?
What is the purpose of the safety fire blanket?
a: To smother fires, including those on a person

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a safety rule in the lab?
What should you do if you are unsure about an experiment step?
Why should you keep flammable liquids away from heat sources?
What is the correct way to handle a hot beaker?
What does the 'Explosive' symbol warn about?
a: Substances that can explode under heat or pressure

questions.q: If you see a sign with a 'High Voltage' symbol, what should you do?
a: Touch it to see if it works

questions.q: What should you do with chemical waste after an experiment?
a: Follow teacher instructions for proper disposal

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to have cluttered workstations?
a: It increases the risk of accidents and spills
It is hard to find pencils

questions.q: What do you use in case of a small fire on the lab bench?
Which rule prevents the spread of bacteria in the lab?
a: Use as many chemicals as possible
Keep personal items on the lab bench

questions.q: What should you look for on a chemical bottle before using it?
Why should you wear an apron in the lab?
a: To protect clothing from spills and stains

questions.q: What should you do if your lab goggles fog up?
a: Ask the teacher to help clean them

questions.q: What does an 'Exclamation mark' hazard symbol usually indicate?
Why is it important to report even minor injuries?
a: To ensure proper care and safety records

questions.q: What should you do if an experiment results in a chemical reaction that you did not expect?
a: Stop immediately and inform the teacher

questions.q: Which item is specifically used to flush eyes if a chemical gets into them?
Why must containers be labeled clearly?
a: To know what is inside and handle it safely
To count how many containers there are

questions.q: What should you do when finished with your experiment?
a: Leave the mess for the next class
Clean up your area and return equipment

questions.q: What is the best way to prevent accidents in the lab?
a: Being careful and following all safety rules
